key_insight: FUSE improves simulation-based posterior estimation by using a dual-track multimodal flow-matching design and FK-steered sampling to better model complex parameter–observation relationships.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more accurate and efficient inference pipeline for scientific models with multimodal or degenerate posteriors, which is valuable in computational physics and astrophysics workflows.
method: Dual-track architecture preserves separate structure for parameters and observations while enabling controlled interaction.
Feynman-Kac-steered sampling uses intermediate observation likelihoods to guide generative trajectories.
Flow matching is used to learn posterior generation without relying on brute-force fusion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that FUSE outperforms state-of-the-art SBI baselines on standard benchmarks and matches ground-truth MCMC closely, including a real exoplanet orbital estimation task with strong parameter degeneracy.
watch_item: The added sampling guidance and dual-track design may increase implementation complexity and require careful tuning of intermediate likelihood estimates.
paper_title: FUSE: FK-Steered Multi-Modal Flow Matching for Efficient Simulation-Based Posterior Estimation
